subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey reject, skip, queue, or remain parallel by default, and should any 409 behavior be opt-in?
rationale: The desired behavior changes externally observable webhook status codes, retry behavior, session-state admission, and security-sensitive liveness disclosure, so source inspection cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Add an opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Preserve current 200/runId behavior by default and add an explicit mapping or request policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics after auth and session-key-prefix checks.

options.title: Fold this into queued webhook ingestion
options.body: Use #100939/#100940 as the canonical design for durable backlog, concurrency, and inspection before adding a separate same-session 409 mode.

options.title: Make 409 the default
options.body: Adopt the issue’s proposed non-2xx behavior for overlapping sessions and accept the compatibility and retry-contract migration burden.

recommendation.title: Add an opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Preserve current 200/runId behavior by default and add an explicit mapping or request policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics after auth and session-key-prefix checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is around isolated cron/session-key routing and hook-agent session behavior, which is the policy surface this issue changes.
